text:
liam: quick heads-up — I reproduced a weird divergence when we re-insert a system prompt mid-generation on the quant3 build
maya: ugh. which model + quant flags?
liam: magnet-13b-q3-rotaryfix (experimental int3 hybrid). sequence length 32k. baseline float32 run is fine, quant3 shows token mismatch after ~1.2k generated tokens when we do a system prompt reinjection.
kevin: can you paste a minimal repro?
liam: steps below (super small):
```
# run baseline float
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.dev/v1/generate -d '{"model":"magnet-13b-fp32","messages":[{"role":"system","content":"<S>system</S>"},{"role":"user","content":"long-user-chunk"}]}'
# run quant3
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.dev/v1/generate -d '{"model":"magnet-13b-q3","messages":[{"role":"system","content":"<S>system</S>"},{"role":"user","content":"long-user-chunk"}]}'
# then mid-stream inject another system prompt before continuing generation
```
liam: diff shows drift in next-token probabilities leading to token insertion/skip at around token 1213. Not consistent every run but high enough freq to be worrying.
maya: suspicious — sounds like a KV cache pointer (RoPE) misalignment when the system prompt is replayed into the cache vs expected prefix. Did you try with and without rotary rescale patch?
liam: yes, rescale toggle flips behavior. with rescale=on it's much less frequent. with rescale=off it's immediate.
kevin: what's the exact reproduction payload? any special whitespace or control tokens in the system prompt?
liam: system prompt includes structured markers and a trailing newline. Example: "<SYS>user meta</SYS>\n". I also tried removing the markers and it's still flaky.
maya: interesting. could be RoPE anchor mismatch if we replay a short system prompt between priming and continuation — especially with quant rounding of offsets.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: canary image magnet-13b-q3-rotaryfix:2026-03-20 deployed to canary pool #b.
liam: I ran a quick log dump from the canary:
```
[2026-03-20T14:02:12Z] kv_index: 0 -> 1212
[2026-03-20T14:02:12Z] rope_anchor: 0x7f3a -> 0x7f2f (delta -13)
[2026-03-20T14:02:12Z] token(out): " the"
[2026-03-20T14:02:12Z] token(expected): " then"
```
liam: the anchor delta seems correlated with the quantized kernel memo pointers (we saw -13 drift).
maya: hypothesis: quantized KV storage uses a block packing that introduces small pointer rounding when we insert short tokens midstream, causing the RoPE position mapping to shift. That would flip the phase on some heads and cause downstream token divergence.
kevin: to prove: we should (a) run identical inputs but pad system prompt to align to pack boundary, (b) run with an artificially re-anchored rope (i.e., reapply exact float anchor offsets after injection), (c) compare logits pre/post injection.
liam: I already tried (a) — padding to 64b boundaries reduces bug freq drastically. good signal.
maya: good. can you open a small canary with a test harness that logs: kv_index, rope_anchor, head_phase_checksum, and next-token logits for first 10 candidates? keep it noisy but short.
liam: will do. plan: create a 10k token long run with system prompt insertion at token 5000 and 8000, run 20 trials each baseline/fp32/q3/q3-rescale. collect diffs.
kevin: add a variant with quant4 hybrid too. may be easier to compare. also run on dedicated gpu (no nvlink jitter)
maya: also include a run where we use the "prefix_cache_disable": true flag to force re-computation instead of KV replay — if that fixes it then it's definitely KV packing.
liam: timeline: I can produce canary + logs by EOD, will post condensed diffs.
kevin: if confirmed, fix ideas: change KV block allocator to maintain stable anchor offsets for small insertions, or add a lightweight re-anchor step after any system prompt reinsertion.
maya: agree. also file a regression test in our context-regression-suite that exercises mid-stream prompt insertion.
liam: filing now: https://redwood.internal/issue/ML-encache-942 (draft) — will drop raw logs there.
kevin: thanks. tagging @sre for canary pool parity check.
maya: nice repro, thanks liam. let's sync if the canary indicates stable root cause. :mag:
_review_notes: generated slack thread about RoPE/KV cache divergence during system-prompt reinsertion; includes short commands and logs. all messages are short and slack style per agents.md
